phrase: I just wanna buy myself one more
note: The 'one more' mindset of corporate bitcoin treasuries. Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy), led by Michael Saylor, kept announcing fresh bitcoin purchases through the 2024-25 bull run, funded by selling shares and borrowing.

phrase:
I take the debt
It’s uncollateralised
note: Strategy's convertible notes are unsecured: no specific asset is pledged as collateral. Lenders are betting on the company, and really on bitcoin, rather than holding a claim on property.
Companies can raise cash by issuing new shares, often through an 'at-the-market' program that sells stock gradually. Strategy used this alongside debt to buy bitcoin, diluting existing shareholders.
A convertible bond is a loan that can turn into company shares if the share price rises enough. In November 2024 Strategy sold US$3 billion of these notes and used the money to buy bitcoin.
Those notes paid 0% interest. Investors gave up regular payments for the chance to convert into shares later, which made it very cheap money for buying bitcoin.
Fiat money is government-issued currency backed by no commodity. Borrowing it at zero interest to buy a scarce asset looks like a glitch: the debt is owed in money that keeps losing value.
Strategy trades on the Nasdaq stock exchange under the ticker MSTR, giving ordinary share investors indirect exposure to bitcoin.

phrase: Stock ticker now is a meme
note: A meme stock trades on online hype and community excitement as much as on business results. MSTR became a retail-trader favourite, often treated as a turbocharged bet on bitcoin.

US spot bitcoin ETFs began trading in January 2024, letting people buy bitcoin exposure through ordinary brokerage and retirement accounts. They took in roughly US$36 billion of net inflows in their first year.

Orange is Bitcoin's signature colour, from its logo. Retirees getting exposed to 'the orange' means pension and retirement funds quietly holding bitcoin through ETFs, sometimes without savers realising.

phrase: Upload your brain to the AI nearest me
note: Mind uploading, copying a person's mind into a computer, is still science fiction. Real brain-computer interfaces are far more limited: Neuralink's first human patient, implanted in 2024, moves a cursor by thought.
In computing, a sandbox is a sealed-off environment where software runs without touching the real system. For an uploaded mind, it is a digital enclosure: a simulation inside a simulation.
Futurist Clif High uses 'sci-fi world' for a coming era he links to AI, precious metals, crypto and the end of fiat money. A circular economy is one where value keeps cycling around a closed network.
A farewell to a human left behind: wiped out in a dystopian future, or uploaded into the machine. Either way, gone into a matrix within a matrix.
Jamie Dimon, CEO of JPMorgan Chase, once called bitcoin a 'fraud'. Being liquid means having cash, or assets easily turned into cash, the very service big banks sell.
Mark Zuckerberg's Meta is building augmented-reality glasses. In 2024 it showed Orion, a prototype that projects holographic images over the real world.

phrase: Altman sell me out a bot
note: Sam Altman leads OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT. AI chatbots and assistants are now sold to the public by monthly subscription.

phrase: Elon let me go to Mars
note: Elon Musk's SpaceX is developing its Starship rocket with the stated goal of carrying people to Mars.

phrase: I got there without any body
note: The upload dream taken literally: the mind arrives as data while the physical body stays behind, or no longer exists at all.

phrase: Bob went off and asked Alice
note: Alice and Bob are the classic placeholder names in cryptography, used to explain how two parties exchange secure messages. Bitcoin's technical writing still uses them.
A CAPTCHA is the puzzle websites use to check you're human, like picking every square with a traffic light. Modern AI can often solve them, which defeats the point.
An LLM, or large language model, is the AI behind chatbots like ChatGPT: software trained on huge amounts of text to predict and generate words.
Prompt injection is an attack where hidden instructions inside text or images trick an AI into ignoring its rules, leaking data or doing things its user never asked for.
AGI, or artificial general intelligence, is hypothetical AI that could match humans at almost any task, not just one narrow job.

phrase:
Computer code stay solvent
Longer than these human beings
Can be rational
note: Flips an old market saying often credited to economist John Maynard Keynes: 'The market can remain irrational longer than you can remain solvent.' Here the machines outlast human patience.

phrase: Cause I just wanna be immortal
note: Radical life extension is a real Silicon Valley pursuit. Billionaire Peter Thiel pledged US$3.5 million to the Methuselah Foundation in 2006 to fund research aimed at reversing ageing.
Regenerative medicine aims to repair or replace damaged tissue; nanotechnology engineers materials at the scale of molecules. Both feature heavily in anti-ageing research and its sci-fi promises.

phrase:
Secure the bag
At an all time high
note: An all-time high is the highest price an asset has ever reached. Bitcoin set a record of about US$126,000 on 6 October 2025. Securing the bag means cashing in at the top.

phrase: For a pound of the flesh
note: From Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, where a lender demands a pound of flesh as payment. It means a harsh price paid in full, here, quite literally, for a new body.

phrase: Printed and woven inside of the lab
note: Bioprinting uses 3D printers loaded with living cells to build tissue layer by layer. Simple tissues can be printed today; working organs and limbs remain experimental.
'Chad' is internet slang for a supremely confident, alpha type. In crypto memes the chad buys and holds calmly while everyone else panics.
'Brokie' is slang for someone who is broke. 'Bots' are automated or copycat accounts, here the crowd left grumbling in the comments.

phrase:
Stuck in the traffic
Punching the dash
note: Immortality spent: every bitcoin gone on becoming superhuman, the stack back to zero, and an ordinary human body stuck in peak-hour traffic.
